old_caption: The video captures a serene and tranquil scene of a mountainous landscape reflected in a calm body of water. The sky is a deep blue, suggesting either early morning or late evening light. In the background, majestic snow-capped mountains rise against the horizon, their peaks sharp and clear. Closer to the foreground, a dense forest of dark green trees lines the shore, adding depth and contrast to the scene. A layer of mist hovers low over the water's surface, creating a soft, ethereal atmosphere that enhances the stillness of the environment. The water itself is perfectly still, acting as a mirror that reflects the mountains and the surrounding trees, doubling the beauty of the landscape. There are no visible animals or characters in the video; it focuses entirely on the natural elements. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, allowing viewers to fully absorb the peaceful and untouched nature of the setting.

caption: The video captures a fixed dawn landscape where a calm lake fills the foreground and snow-dusted peaks line the horizon, reflected in the mostly still water. A horizontal band of low mist hovers over the surface, continuously reshaping as wisps thin and thicken near the shoreline and the mountain bases. A forested shore sits on the right and a dark hill on the left, holding their positions while the camera stays steady. A small bright point appears in the misty mid-ground on the left and drifts gradually rightward toward the centre before fading. Faint linear ripples disturb the left foreground water at intervals, spreading briefly then settling while the mountain reflection stays largely intact. The pale blue sky above the peaks remains essentially unchanged, with a tiny bright dot moving across the upper sky. The framing remains steady, keeping the mirrored peaks and drifting mist as dominant elements. The clip thus presents an ongoing, quiet reshaping of mist and surface rather than a single completed action.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.

the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

draft_caption: The video captures a fixed dawn landscape where a calm lake fills the foreground and snow-dusted peaks line the horizon, mirrored in the still water. A horizontal band of low mist hovers over the surface, continuously reshaping as wisps thin and thicken near the shoreline and the mountain bases. A forested shore sits on the right and a dark hill on the left, holding their positions while the camera stays steady. A small bright point emerges in the misty mid-ground on the left and drifts gradually rightward toward the centre before growing indistinct. Faint linear ripples disturb the left foreground water at intervals, spreading briefly then settling while the mountain reflection stays largely intact. The pale blue sky above the peaks lightens only imperceptibly, with a tiny dot near the highest summit. The framing does not change, keeping the mirrored peaks and drifting mist as dominant elements. The clip thus presents an ongoing, quiet reshaping of mist and surface rather than a single completed action.
